statement: `hibernation_available()` is a four-term conjunction: hibernation not disabled on the command line, no lockdown covering `LOCKDOWN_HIBERNATION`, no live secretmem file, no active CXL memory. Five sites read it: `hibernate()` returns `-EPERM` (766-769), `software_resume_initcall` returns 0 (1111-1112), `disk_show()` prints `[disabled]` (1168-1169), `disk_store()` returns `-EPERM` (1211-1212) and `resume_store()` returns the byte count without acting (1269-1270).

`nohibernate` sets both `noresume = 1` and `nohibernate = 1`, so one token removes the `disk` target and the boot-time image read together; unlike `noresume` (HA4) it cannot be undone from userspace, because `disk_store()` refuses with `-EPERM` while the predicate is false (1211-1212). The documentation says the same in one line (S336 4479).

statement: `hibernate=` is an ordered prefix parse: `noresume` (1426-1427), `nocompress` (1428-1429), bare `no` (1430-1432), `protect_image` (1433-1435). `hibernate=nocompress` only stops compression and does not disable; `hibernate=no` — and any value starting `no` that is not `noresume*`/`nocompress*`, including a typo such as `hibernate=non` or a would-be `hibernate=noprotect_image` — sets both `noresume` and `nohibernate`. Unknown values match no branch and are ignored.

`noresume` sets only `noresume`: `hibernation_available()` never reads it, so `hibernate()` still runs (766-769), but `software_resume_initcall` returns 0 on `noresume || !hibernation_available()` (1111-1112) — an image written by the last hibernation is not read at the next boot. The documentation states it as disabling resume and restoring original swap space (S336 4593-4594).

`LOCKDOWN_HIBERNATION` (index 5) precedes `LOCKDOWN_INTEGRITY_MAX` (index 21); `lockdown_param` stores exactly those sentinels for the two levels (`lockdown_levels[] = {LOCKDOWN_NONE, LOCKDOWN_INTEGRITY_MAX, LOCKDOWN_CONFIDENTIALITY_MAX}`, S345 20-22), and `lockdown_is_locked_down()` returns `-EPERM` when `kernel_locked_down >= what` (S345 65-70) — so `integrity` already blocks hibernation, not only `confidentiality`. The sysfs file lists one label per selectable level, which is why it has three words.
